name: Koro Nulu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only SIL socioling survey (Decker et al. 2021, wordlist) and two short MA feature studies; no phonology/grammar with stress found.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Samuel Eju, Adedamola Aregbesola, Fittokka Gobak, Andrew Lewinan, Luther Hon & Thelma Araokanmi. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Koro Nulu [vkn] and Koro Zuba [vkz], formerly Ija-Zuba [vki], Languages of Central Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-051. Dallas: SIL International. 49 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 8.3.2 gives only tentative consonant/vowel inventories from the 348-item wordlist; Appendix D (p.35): 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis done of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Sec. 4 'Previous research' lists only Temple 1919, Gunn & Conant 1960, Obatoye 2011 and Blench 2014 (mention).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2020. Change Request 2020-032 (Aregbesola, Hon, Danladi, SIL Nigeria): split Ija-Zuba [vki] into Koro Nulu [vkn] and Koro Zuba [vkz]; with New Code Request forms for vkn and vkz.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; names, locations, 7% lexical similarity Nulu-Zuba, sources (Decker et al. forthcoming, Blench 2014).

sources.citation: Adebayo, Funke Christiana. 2011. Aspects of question formation in Ija-Koro [Ìjà-Kórò]. B.A. long essay, University of Ilorin (07/15CB012), May 2011. [same Jili-like 'Ija-Koro' lect as Yusuf 2011; identity doubtful]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Generic mention of stress as a suprasegmental category only; brief sound inventory and tone marking; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Bakare, Bimbo Mary. 2011. Aspects of Koro morphology. B.A. long essay, Department of Linguistics and Nigerian Languages, University of Ilorin (matric 07/15CB046), June 2011. viii+95 pp. [Glottolog ref 547181; language of Ija-Koro, Tafa LGA; lexicon matches SIL Koro Nulu wordlist]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Sec. 2.6-2.7 (pp. 50-51): three level tones H, M, L plus a falling contour tone, with tone-pattern examples (H, HH, HL, LML, LL, LHM, LH); sec. 2.8 syllable structure CV, CVV, VCV.

sources.citation: Obatoye, Julianah Folasade. 2011. The Koro-Ija noun phrase. B.A. long essay, Department of Linguistics and Nigerian Languages, University of Ilorin (07/15CB068), May 2011. [Glottolog ref 319684; data collected at Ija-Koro village, Tafa LGA; cited by Decker et al. 2021 as on Koro Nulu]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 2.1.5 'Tone System in Koro-Ija Language' (p.38): 'Koro a Niger-Congo language is tonal. The language attests to register tones' -- High, Low, Mid (unmarked), with minimal pair énwé 'sun' / ènwé 'day'; syllable types, no coda.

sources.citation: Yusuf, Stephen Kunle. 2011. Aspects of Ija-Koro [Ìjá-Kórò] phonology. B.A. long essay, Department of Linguistics and Nigerian Languages, University of Ilorin (07/15CB107), May 2011. [not in Glottolog; IDENTITY DOUBTFUL -- lexicon (etí 'head', oto 'ear', ekwere 'water', ovóó 'goat', nààre 'four', ezan 'blood', aku 'bone') matches the Rjili/Tanjijili [uji] column of Decker et al. 2021, not the Koro Nulu column]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only a generic textbook line listing 'tones, intonation, stress, length' as suprasegmentals (sec. 2.2); ch. 4: tone language with three register tones H, M, L, tone phonemic, no tone spreading/stability; syllables N, CV, V, no closed syllables. No statement about stress in the language.

sources.citation: SIL Nigeria survey team (Hon, Luther et al.). 2019. Koro Nulu 348-item wordlist audio recordings and field transcriptions, Ija village, 23 Oct 2019 (underlying data of JLSR 2021-051).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only primary phonetic data on Koro Nulu proper; any future prosodic (tone/stress) analysis would have to start here; not published beyond the Appendix D transcription.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2014. The Jijili (Koro) language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Ms., Kay Williamson Educational Foundation (wordlist paper; mentions Koro-Ija and Koro-Zuba).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other linguistic work naming Koro Ija/Nulu; would confirm whether Blench holds any Koro Nulu data with tone/stress notes (unlikely) and helps settle the identity of the Jili-like 'Ija-Koro' lect in Yusuf 2011.
